Rashi on Chullin 86a:11:1.hebrew: סיפא אמרי בשרא הוא דלא מבעיא ליה - הרואה שאין שוחטין בנו אחריו, אין מבין שמשום אותו ואת בנו הוא, אלא אומר: אינו צריך לבשר:
Rashi on Chullin 86a:11:1.english: [With regard to] the latter clause, they will say it is meat that he does not need - One who sees that they do not slaughter its offspring after it does not realize that it is because of [the prohibition of] "it and its offspring," rather he says: "He does not need meat":

Rashi on Chullin 86a:11:2.hebrew: רישא נמי - ליחייבוהו לרואה לכסות מספק, ואפ"ה לא אתי למיכל מיניה, דאמרי: כסוי זה אינו אלא כדי לנקר חצרו:
Rashi on Chullin 86a:11:2.english: The first clause as well - Let them obligate one who sees [the slaughter] to cover [the blood] out of doubt, and even so, one will not come to eat from it, for [people] will say: this covering is only in order to clean his courtyard:

Rashi on Chullin 86a:12:1.hebrew: הכי גרסי' שחט באשפה מאי איכא למימר - שחט באשפה, הכל יודעים שהכסוי לאו לנקר הוא:
Rashi on Chullin 86a:12:1.english: This is the reading: [If] he slaughtered in a garbage dump, what is there to say - [If] he slaughtered in a garbage dump, everyone knows that the covering [of the blood] is not to clean [the area]:

Rashi on Chullin 86a:12:2.hebrew: אם בא לימלך - לבית דין, הרואה ששחטו והדם מגולה, ואמר: "כלום אני חייב לכסות?", ואנו אומרים לו: "כסה", אומר בלבו שהיא שחיטה, ואתי למיכל:
Rashi on Chullin 86a:12:2.english: If [one] comes to consult - the court: [namely,] one who sees that they slaughtered [an animal] and the blood is uncovered, and he says, "Am I obligated to cover [it]?" and we say to him, "Cover [it]," he will think to himself that it is a [valid] slaughter and come to eat [from it]:

Rashi on Chullin 86a:13:1.hebrew: סיפא נמי בא לימלך - "מה אני לשחוט אחריהם את בנו?", ואנו אומרים לו: "אסור", הוא סבור שהיא שחיטה:
Rashi on Chullin 86a:13:1.english: The latter clause as well, [if one] comes to consult - "What [is the law regarding] my slaughtering its offspring after them?" and we say to him, "[It is] forbidden," he will think that it is a [valid] slaughter:

Rashi on Chullin 86a:14:1.hebrew: אלא רבנן - לאו להכי חיישי, וברישא נמי פליגי:
Rashi on Chullin 86a:14:1.english: Rather, the Rabbis - They are not concerned about this, and they disagree in the first clause [regarding covering the blood] as well:

Rashi on Chullin 86a:15:1.english: Stringently - In a matter of doubt, we rule stringently:

Rashi on Chullin 86a:16:1.hebrew: מחייב - מלקות, דסבירא ליה ודאי נבלה היא, והאוכלה לוקה:
Rashi on Chullin 86a:16:1.english: [He] would deem liable - [to receive] lashes, for he holds [that] it is definitely an animal carcass, and one who eats it receives lashes:

Rashi on Chullin 86a:17:1.hebrew: מאי איריא רוב אפילו מיעוט - מעשיהם מקולקלין ורובן מתוקנין, הוה פשיטא לן דנבלה היא לר"מ, דהא שמעינן ליה דחייש למיעוטא, וסמוך מיעוטא לחזקה, שבהמה זו בחזקת איסור אבר מן החי היתה עומדת, ולא נודע לך שנשחטה:
Rashi on Chullin 86a:17:1.english: Why [did he] specifically [say] a majority? Even [if] a minority - [of] their actions are bungled and the majority of them are proper, it would be obvious to us that it is a carcass according to Rabbi Meir, for we have heard him [say] that he is concerned for a minority; and append the minority to the presumptive status, for this animal stood in a presumptive status of the prohibition of a limb from a living animal, and it has not become known to you that it was [properly] slaughtered:

Rashi on Chullin 86a:17:2.english: And the majority is weakened - [namely, the majority of] their proper actions:

Rashi on Chullin 86a:18:1.english: As we learned - [a case] like this [where a minority is combined with a presumptive status]:

Rashi on Chullin 86a:18:2.hebrew: שדרכו של תינוק לטפח - ידיו באשפות ששרצים מצויים שם, וטימא את העיסה, שאנו רואין שנגע בה:
Rashi on Chullin 86a:18:2.english: [Because] it is the manner of a child to dabble - his hands in garbage heaps, where creeping things are commonly found, and [thus] he rendered the dough impure, since we see that he touched it:

Rashi on Chullin 86a:1:1.hebrew: לא מיבעיא קאמר - רב דימי מודה הוא בנחירה דלא בעי כסוי, אלא הכי אמר רב דימי: דבצא טרוף סגיא, וכל שכן בצא נחור:
Rashi on Chullin 86a:1:1.english: [The Gemara] is speaking [in the style of:] "It is not necessary" - Rav Dimi agrees regarding tearing loose [the windpipe and gullet] that it does not require covering [the blood]; rather, this is what Rav Dimi said: that with "Go out [and] render [it] a tereifa" it suffices [to exempt it from covering], and all the more so with "Go out [and] tear [it] loose."

Rashi on Chullin 86a:3:1.hebrew: אימא זו היא שחיטתו - קא משמע לן "צא נחור", ורבי לטעמיה, דאמר יש שחיטה לעוף מ"כאשר צויתיך":
Rashi on Chullin 86a:3:1.english: I would say [that] this is its slaughter - [Therefore] he teaches us: "Go out [and] tear loose [its windpipe and gullet]," and Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] follows his own reasoning, as he says [that] slaughter applies to a bird [by Torah law, derived] from [the verse], "As I have commanded you":

Rashi on Chullin 86a:4:1.english: And could moths have infested his flax - [that] of Rabbi Chiyya:

Rashi on Chullin 86a:4:2.hebrew: בני הגולה - לאו אנשי כנסת הגדולה קאמר, אלא בהנך דורות אחרונים קאמר, שהתחילו ללקות בני ארץ ישראל ביינם ופשתנם מפני שנתקלקלו דורות, ומשעלו מבני בבל לכאן, שהיו חסידים, פסקו כאן הזועות:
Rashi on Chullin 86a:4:2.english: The people of the Exile - [He] does not mean the Men of the Great Assembly; rather, he is speaking of those later generations, when the inhabitants of the Land of Israel began to be stricken in their wine and their flax because the generations had become corrupted, and once [some] of the people of Babylonia, who were pious, ascended here [to the Land of Israel], the earthquakes ceased here:

Rashi on Chullin 86a:4:3.hebrew: ונתנו חכמים עיניהם ברבי חייא ובניו - שבזכותם באתה טובה זאת. רבי חייא ובניו מבבל עלו, כדאמרי' בשילהי פ"ק דסוכה (דף כ.):
Rashi on Chullin 86a:4:3.english: And the Sages placed their eyes on Rabbi Ḥiyya and his sons - [meaning] that through their merit this good [fortune] came about. Rabbi Ḥiyya and his sons ascended from Babylonia, as we say at the end of the first chapter of Sukkah (20a):

Rashi on Chullin 86a:4:4.english: Meteors, earthquakes, thunder, and winds - It is explained in Berakhot, in [the chapter] HaRo'eh (Berakhot 59a), that all of them are for a curse:

Rashi on Chullin 86a:4:6.english: Winds - A tempest, [in Old French:] estorbeillon [whirlwind]:

Rashi on Chullin 86a:5:1.english: In accordance with [the statement of] Rav Yehuda - who said [that] the merit of the righteous is effective for others, and not for themselves in this world:

Rashi on Chullin 86a:5:2.hebrew: חנינא בני - הוא רבי חנינא בן דוסא, ובימיו היה קול זה יוצא:
Rashi on Chullin 86a:5:2.english: Chanina, My son - He is Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa, and in his days this voice would emerge:

Rashi on Chullin 86a:5:3.english: A kav of carobs is sufficient - [he] sustains himself in hardship and scarcity:

Rashi on Chullin 86a:6:1.hebrew: ואחרים רואין אותן - דאמרן בריש מכילתין (דף ב.) דשחיטתן כשרה, אותן אחרים חייבין לכסות, כדתנן לקמן (חולין דף פז.): "שחט ולא כסה וראהו אחר, חייב לכסות":
Rashi on Chullin 86a:6:1.english: And others see them - Since we said at the beginning of our tractate (2a) that their slaughter is valid, those others are obligated to cover [the blood], as we learned in a Mishnah later on (Chullin 87a): "If one slaughtered and did not cover [the blood], and another saw him, he is obligated to cover [it]."

Rashi on Chullin 86a:6:2.hebrew: פטור מלכסות - וטעמא מפרש בגמ', דר"מ חשיב ליה כנבלה גמורה:
Rashi on Chullin 86a:6:2.english: Exempt from covering [the blood] - And the reason is explained in the Gemara, for Rabbi Meir considers it like a complete nevelah [unslaughtered carcass]:

Rashi on Chullin 86a:7:1.hebrew: וחכמים אוסרין - שמא יפה שחטו, והויא לה שחיטה מעלייתא:
Rashi on Chullin 86a:7:1.english: And the Sages prohibit [it] - lest they slaughtered properly, and it is a valid slaughter:

Rashi on Chullin 86a:7:2.english: That he does not incur [the forty lashes] - because it is an uncertain warning:

Rashi on Chullin 86a:8:1.english: What is different [about] the first clause, where they do not disagree - and [why do they not] obligate [one] to cover [the blood] out of doubt:

Tosafot on Chullin 86a:10:1.hebrew: סיפא נמי כיון דאמרי רבנן אסור לשחוט אחריהם אמרי שחיטה מעלייתא היא - תימה, דמשום גזירה דלמא אתי למיכל נבלה יש לי להתיר לאו דאותו ואת בנו מספק? מה לי לאו דאותו ואת בנו ומה לי לאו דנבלה? ולא דמי לרישא דפטרינן לכסות מספק, דשב ואל תעשה בעלמא הוא, ודלמא אתי למיכל. ויש לומר, דאי לאו דרוב מעשיהם מקולקלים, לא היו פוטרים מלכסות משום גזרה דלמא אתי למיכל; אלא שלא נחמיר להטעין כסוי, אמרי' דפטור משום דדלמא אתי למיכל. וכיון דרוב מעשיהם מקולקלין, יש לנו להתיר נמי לשחוט אחריהם דלמא אתי למיכל:
Tosafot on Chullin 86a:10:1.english: The latter clause as well, since the Rabbis say it is prohibited to slaughter after them, they will say it is a proper slaughter - This is astonishing: because of a decree lest one come to eat nevelah [an improperly slaughtered animal], should I permit the negative prohibition of "it and its offspring" out of doubt? What is [the difference] to me [between] the negative prohibition of "it and its offspring" and the negative prohibition of nevelah? And it is not similar to the first clause, where we exempt [him] from covering [the blood] out of doubt, for that is merely [a matter of] "sit and do not act," and [there is the concern] lest one come to eat [from their slaughter]. And one can say: if it were not that most of their actions are improper, they would not have exempted [him] from covering [the blood] because of a decree lest one come to eat; rather, [the Gemara means] that we should not be stringent to require covering [the blood] — we say that he is exempt because [of the concern] lest one come to eat. And since most of their actions are improper, we should also permit slaughtering after them [because of the concern] lest one come to eat:

Tosafot on Chullin 86a:16:1.hebrew: מאי טעמא דר' מאיר הואיל ורוב מעשיהן מקולקלין - הקשה הר"ר שמואל מוורדין: ורבנן מאי טעמייהו? אם רוב מעשיהם מתוקנין, א"כ יהא מותר לאכול משחיטתם, ועוד: השוחט אחריהם אמאי אינו סופג ארבעים? ואי פלגא ופלגא, אם סמוך פלגא דמקולקלין לחזקה דעומד בחזקת איסור ואיתרע ליה מחצה דמתוקנים — אם כן יהא מותר לשחוט אחריהם, וגם יתחייבו על שחיטתן משום נבלה! וי"ל: דמספקא להו לרבנן אי רוב מעשיהם מקולקלין, אי רוב מעשיהם מתוקנין; והשתא לא מהניא חזקה מידי. ולרבי מאיר פשיטא ליה דרוב מעשיהם מקולקלין. ואם תאמר: ואף על גב דרוב מעשיהם מקולקלין, מ"מ רבי מאיר, כיון דחייש למיעוטא, אמאי לקי משום נבלה, ואמאי מותר לשחוט אחריהם? וי"ל: דסמוך חזקה לרוב מקולקלין, והוה ליה מיעוטא דמתוקנין מיעוטא דמיעוטא, ולמיעוטא דמיעוטא לא חייש רבי מאיר:
Tosafot on Chullin 86a:16:1.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Meir? Since the majority of their actions are bungled - Rabbi Shmuel of Verdun raised a difficulty: And the Rabbis, what is their reason? If the majority of their actions are performed properly, if so, it should be permitted to eat from their slaughter; and furthermore, why does one who slaughters after them not incur forty [lashes]? And if [it is] half and half — if [so], append the half of bungled [actions] to the presumptive status [of the animal], which stands in a presumptive status of prohibition, and the half of proper [actions] is [thereby] weakened; if so, it should be permitted to slaughter after them, and they should also be liable [to lashes] for [eating] their slaughter due to [the prohibition of] an animal carcass! And one can say that the Rabbis are in doubt whether the majority of their actions are bungled or whether the majority of their actions are performed properly, and now the presumptive status is of no avail at all. Whereas to Rabbi Meir, it is clear that the majority of their actions are bungled. And if you say: Even though the majority of their actions are bungled, nevertheless, since Rabbi Meir is concerned for a minority, why does one incur lashes [for eating their slaughter] due to [the prohibition of] an animal carcass, and why is it permitted to slaughter after them? And one can say: Append the presumptive status to the majority of bungled [actions], and the minority of proper [actions] becomes a minority of a minority; and for a minority of a minority, Rabbi Meir is not concerned:

Tosafot on Chullin 86a:18:1.hebrew: רוב תינוקות מטפחים - פי' בקונטרס: מטפחים באשפות, אבל בעיסה ודאי נגע, שהרי העיסה בידו. ור"ת מפרש דרוב תינוקות מטפחים בעיסה, דטיפוח שייך באוכלים ומשקין, כדאמרינן בע"ז בפרק רבי ישמעאל (עבודה זרה דף ס:): "או שהיה מטפח ע"פ חבית". וכן איתא בירושלמי בהדיא: "מפני שדרכו של תינוקות לטפח בעיסה". אבל תינוק ודאי טמא, דסתם תינוקות ודאי טמאים, דאמרי' בתוספתא (דטהרות פ"ג) שסתם תינוקות טמאים מפני שנשים נדות מגפפות ומנשקות אותם. ור"מ דמטהר, משום דאית לן למתלי באדם טהור שבא לשם ונטל מן העיסה ונתן לו כדי שלא יטמא העיסה. וכי האי גוונא אמר במס' טהרות בפ"ג (מ"ז) לעיל מהך תינוק דהכא: "תינוק שנמצא בצד בית הקברות ושושנים בידו, אע"פ שאין השושנים אלא ממקום הטומאה, טהור, שאני אומר אדם טהור נתן לו"; אע"פ שסתם תינוק טמא, היינו ממגע נדה, והתם טהור מטומאת מת קאמר. אי נמי, מיירי בתינוק שהוא טהור בודאי, שהניחתו אמו מלוכלך, כדתניא (בתוספתא שם): "תינוק שהניחתו אמו ובאה ומצאתו כמו שהוא — טהור. בד"א? שהניחתו מלוכלך, אבל הניחתו נקי — טמא, מפני שנשים נדות מגפפות ומנשקות אותו". ואף על פי שלא נמצא בצק בידו מטמאים חכמים, דתניא בתוספתא (שם): "תינוק שנמצא עומד בצד קופה של בצק או בצד חבית של משקין — רבי מאיר מטהר וחכמים מטמאין, שדרך התינוק לטפח. אמר רבי יוסי: אם יכול לפשוט ידו וליקח — טמא, ואם לאו — טהור". ולא נקט הכא "בצק בידו" אלא לרבותא דר"מ, דאפילו הכי תולין באדם טהור:
Tosafot on Chullin 86a:18:1.english: A majority of children handle - Rashi explained: they dabble in garbage heaps, but as for the dough, [the child] certainly touched [it], since the dough is in his hand. But Rabbeinu Tam explains that a majority of children dabble in dough, for "patting" [tippuach] applies to foods and liquids, as we say in Avodah Zarah in the chapter [entitled] Rabbi Yishmael (Avodah Zarah 60b): "or if he was patting on the mouth of a barrel." And so it is explicitly [stated] in the Jerusalem Talmud: "because it is the manner of children to pat in dough." However, the child [himself] is certainly impure, for ordinary children are certainly impure, as we say in the Tosefta (Teharot ch. 3) that ordinary children are impure because menstruating women embrace and kiss them. And Rabbi Meir, who deems [the dough] pure, [does so] because we should attribute [the dough in the child's hand] to a pure person who came there, took from the dough, and gave [it] to him so that he would not render the dough impure. And similarly, it states in Tractate Teharot, in chapter 3 (mishna 7), prior to this [mishna of] "a child" here: "A child who was found alongside a cemetery with lilies in his hand — even though the lilies are only from the place of impurity, he is pure, because I say a pure person gave [them] to him"; [and] even though an ordinary child is impure, that is from the touch of a menstruating woman, whereas there it means he is pure from corpse impurity. Alternatively, [that mishna] is speaking of a child who is definitely pure, whom his mother left dirty, as it was taught (in the Tosefta there): "A child whom his mother left, and she came [back] and found him as he was — he is pure. When does this apply? When she left him dirty; but if she left him clean — he is impure, because menstruating women embrace and kiss him." And even if dough was not found in his hand, the Sages deem [the dough] impure, as it was taught in the Tosefta (there): "A child who is found standing alongside a basket of dough or alongside a barrel of liquids — Rabbi Meir deems [it] pure, and the Sages deem [it] impure, because it is the manner of a child to pat. Rabbi Yosei said: If he can stretch out his hand and take [from it], it is impure, and if not, it is pure." And [the mishna] here only mentioned "dough in his hand" to demonstrate the novelty of Rabbi Meir's [ruling], that even so, we attribute [it] to a pure person:
